In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed pipeline collider is a technically and economically feasible option to build an ultimate-energy hadronic collider, with a cost that is comparable with the cost of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
the proposed pipeline collider would enable the realization of an ultimate-energy hadrons collider at a cost that is competitive with that of a conventional collider.
the proposed approach to the construction of the dipole magnets and of the pipeline is technically feasible and would provide the best cost-performance ratio for a future hadron collider.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cost of the dipole is projected to be less than 1/10 that of the present LHC dipoles.
a future collider, based upon the new dipole technology and a pipeline cryostat, could be built at a cost that is an order of magnitude lower than the cost for the present LHC.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of an ultimate-energy hadrons collider, with a total project cost of ∼$5B, and that the cost of such a collider would be dominated by tunnel cost.

a 500-TeV collider is possible with existing accelerator technology.
the cost of a future collider can be reduced by an order of magnitude if the dipole field is optimized for cost.
